descs: Open plough-land, hedge and furrow, gray under a wide sky.

spots.name: Dew-Pond Corner
spots.desc: A dew-pond sits shallow in a fold of ground, its rim trodden hard once by men who drank here the night before the wall broke. The water still tastes faintly of iron, Harrowfield says, though nobody living has proved it.
spots.brief: A shallow dew-pond, its rim long trodden hard.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 5 south and 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 2 south and 1 east, then in.

spots.name: The North Ditch-Crossing
spots.desc: The old ditch runs shallow here before the ground climbs toward the hedge. North, hedgerow gives way to the Fallows' dikes; the road that way carries the name of somebody else's grief now.
spots.brief: The ditch shallows. North: the Fallows' dikes.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 2 south, then in.

spots.name: The High Furrow
spots.desc: Plough-ridges climb toward the field's northern hedge, the soil paler here where flint sits close under the topsoil. Even this far from the lines, the furrows run crooked, as if the ploughman's mind was elsewhere.
spots.brief: Pale, crooked furrows near the hedge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 1 west and 2 south, then in.

spots.name: Crow-Tree Rise
spots.desc: A single ash stands black-branched against the sky, and crows keep it the way a garrison keeps a wall — always at least one watching, however still the rest of the plain goes.
spots.brief: A crow-kept ash; always one watching.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 5 south and 1 west, then south. The Truce Field: 2 west and 2 south, then in.

spots.name: The Reed Margin
spots.desc: Reed and rush still crowd the low ground here, the fen's last reach before the plain firms up for good. The air smells of standing water behind you and turned earth ahead.
spots.brief: Reed gives way to firm plough-land.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 1 south and 2 east, then in.

spots.name: The Horse-Mound
spots.desc: A long, low mound breaks the plough-land here, turf too thick and old for any furrow to have crossed it. Whatever went into it went in whole, and with its tack still on.
spots.brief: A long mound, too old to have been ploughed.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 4 south and 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 1 south and 1 east, then in.

spots.name: The Old Horse-Pit
spots.desc: A wide pit scars the ground beside the mound, its sides slumped soft with age. Bone shows white at the bottom where the rain has had four hundred years to work at it.
spots.brief: A slumped pit, old bone showing white.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 1 south, then in.

spots.name: The Lone Elm
spots.desc: One elm stands where a hedge-line ought to run on, the rest of it long grubbed out for firewood or fencing. Rope-galls scar its lowest limb, healed over crooked.
spots.brief: A lone elm, an old rope-scar on its limb.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 1 west and 1 south, then in.

spots.name: The Beacon Rise
spots.desc: The ground swells toward a ruined signal-tower, built once to carry warning faster than any rider could. Nobody has lit it in longer than Harrowfield can say, though the brazier at its foot still holds char.
spots.brief: Rising ground, a ruined beacon-tower above.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 4 south and 1 west, then south. The Truce Field: 2 west and 1 south, then in.

spots.name: Windrow Bank
spots.desc: Cut hay lies windrowed along the plain's eastern hedge, turned and left for a hay-making that never quite gets finished before the light goes. Somebody's habit, more than anybody's plan.
spots.brief: Windrowed hay along the hedge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 3 west and 1 south, then in.

spots.name: The Last Firm Ground
spots.desc: The ground stops giving underfoot here, reed and standing water behind, sound plough-earth ahead. West, the drove-road picks its way out of Fenmarch's fen toward this same firm rise.
spots.brief: Firm ground at last. West: the drove-road.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 2 east, then in.

spots.name: The Cairn of Bosses
spots.desc: A low cairn of dug earth marks where somebody has been turning up old iron with a spade rather than a plough — and among the spoil, unmistakably, the curved bronze of shield-bosses, three or four, still uncounted.
spots.brief: A dug cairn; shield-bosses among the spoil.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 3 south and 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 1 east, then in.

spots.name: The Boundary Stone
spots.desc: A squared stone marks some old field-boundary, its carved letters worn to guesswork. Someone has propped a second, newer stone beside it, its face still blank, waiting on a mason who hasn't come yet.
spots.brief: An old boundary stone, a blank one beside it.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 3 south and 1 west, then south. The Truce Field lies west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: East Hedge Corner
spots.desc: The plain's hedge turns a hard corner here, thorn grown thick enough to have never once needed mending. Beyond it, country the Shieldings doesn't claim runs on unseen.
spots.brief: A thick hedge-corner, thorn unmended.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field lies west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: Reed's End
spots.desc: The last true reed gives out against a low bank, fen behind, plough-land ahead for good. A heron stands the boundary like it was posted there on purpose.
spots.brief: The fen's last reed; a heron standing guard.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: 1 north and 2 east, then in.

spots.name: The Long Ruts
spots.desc: A cart-track runs straight across the plain here, ruts pressed by four hundred years of stock driven between the fen and the market roads east, indifferent to whatever the ground beneath it remembers.
spots.brief: A straight, rutted drove-track.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 south and 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 1 north and 1 east, then in.

spots.name: The Shield-Ditch, Further On
spots.desc: The old ditch runs on from here, north and west, its line still true enough to walk by moonlight. The field-reeve's plough turns south of it without fail, every season, without anyone telling the new hands why.
spots.brief: The ditch runs on, true by moonlight.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 3 south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Banner-Stump
spots.desc: A blackened stump stands alone where nothing else grew back, wood gone hard as iron. Harrowfield says a banner was planted here once and burned to the root rather than be struck.
spots.brief: A blackened stump; a banner burned to the root.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 south and 1 west, then south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: Far Hedge
spots.desc: The eastern hedge runs thin and gapped here, more suggestion than barrier. Something about the ground beyond it discourages sheep as much as people.
spots.brief: A thin, gapped hedge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 west and 3 south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Fen Verge
spots.desc: Plough-land softens back toward fen at the plain's southwest corner, the last furrows giving up a little earlier every year the dikes go unmended.
spots.brief: Plough-land softening back toward fen.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 3 east and 2 south. The Truce Field: 2 north and 2 east, then in.

spots.name: The Old Chantry Path
spots.desc: A path of flat stones leads toward a second, older chapel roof, moss-black and long neglected by the priest who keeps the newer one. Whatever's kept there, he has never once mentioned it unasked.
spots.brief: A path to an older, neglected chapel.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 1 south and 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 2 north and 1 east, then in.

spots.name: The Turned Furrow
spots.desc: The ploughs turn away from a long strip of ground here, leaving it fallow between two worked fields without a fence or a marker to explain why. Every hand in Harrowfield knows to leave it, and none says the word for what it is.
spots.brief: A fallow strip; the ploughs simply turn away.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 1 south and 1 east, then south. The Truce Field lies north, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: Plough's End
spots.desc: The worked land runs out here, the last furrow trailing off crooked as if the ploughman looked back once too often. North, the ground belongs to older business entirely.
spots.brief: The last furrow, trailing off crooked.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Old Muster Ground
spots.desc: Flattened ground and old fire-scars mark where a camp once stood in some strength, cookfire-black still showing through the turf. In, whatever's left of it keeps its own hours.
spots.brief: Old fire-scars; a camp's flattened ground.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 1 south and 1 west, then south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: South Hedge
spots.desc: The southern hedge runs low and well-kept here, Harrowfield's hand plain in every laid stem. Someone still walks this line every season, whatever else goes untended further out.
spots.brief: A low, well-kept hedge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 west and 2 south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Ditch-Road
spots.desc: A cart-track runs south from the old ditch toward Harrowfield's rooftops, worn by every plough and every funeral the village has sent out this way in living memory.
spots.brief: A cart-track south, toward Harrowfield.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 2 east, then south. The Truce Field: 3 north and 1 east, then in.

spots.name: Harrow's Approach
spots.desc: The plain gives way to hedged closes and the first sound of a dog barking, Harrowfield close now south. The ground here has been worked so long it barely remembers being anything else.
spots.brief: Hedged closes; Harrowfield close south.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 1 east, then south. The Truce Field lies north, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Boundary Hedge
spots.desc: The plain's southeast hedge marks Harrowfield's furthest worked ground, laid and relaid every generation by hands that never once asked what lay north of it.
spots.brief: The southeast hedge, Harrowfield's edge.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is 1 west, then south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

spots.name: The Truce Field's Edge
spots.desc: The plough-land stops here in a straight line nobody drew. Beyond it lies the ground the dead hold, mounds low under the grass and the ditch's dark seam across it. Dusk comes early to it.
spots.brief: The edge of the dead's ground.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield lies south and east, well round the ground the plough won't cross. The Truce Field: here — go in.

spots.name: The Ditch-Gate Field
spots.desc: The last furlong before Harrowfield's ditch-gate, cart-ruts running south into the village and the smell of bread, or its absence, on the wind.
spots.brief: The last furlong before the gate.

actions.label: get your bearings
fx: As the plain runs, Harrowfield is here — go south. The Truce Field lies north and west, well round the ground the plough won't cross.

onEnter: Gray as frost, a shape stands its ground where the light says nothing should be standing at all — a levy who never stood down, still holding a line that broke four hundred years ago.

vars.NAME: the Horse-Barrow
vars.SIGN: Bit and bridle-rings, corroded to lace, are heaped just inside the doorstone — offerings, or the last of somebody's tack.
vars.LOOT: a cavalry officer's spurs, silver gone black

vars.NAME: the Levies' Beacon
vars.VIEW: the whole Shieldings spreads flat and gray below, the old ditch a dark seam across it, Harrowfield's smoke low to the south
vars.SIGN: Cold char still fills the brazier at its foot, banked for one fire yet to come.
vars.LOOT: a signaller's tinder-horn, dry inside still

vars.NAME: the Chantry Bone-House
vars.SIGN: Older bones are stacked here too, tidy and forgotten — a fever, forty years back, Elgin never spoke of.

vars.NAME: the Founders' Camp
vars.SIGN: A charter-stone, blank now, is set flat into the ground by the fire-ring — something was once nailed to it, and read aloud.
vars.LOOT: a Free Companies recruiting seal, unbroken

sh_horsebarrow_castoff.name: a snapped stirrup-leather
sh_horsebarrow_castoff.hint: the buckle's still good; whoever it threw didn't come back for it

sh_beacon_castoff.name: a coil of signal-rope, frayed through
sh_beacon_castoff.hint: frayed clean through; whatever it was raising, it stopped partway

sh_horse_barrow_rathe.name: Rathe
sh_horse_barrow_rathe.desc: A farrier, kit bag over one shoulder, keeping the sort of distance from the doorstone that isn't quite fear and isn't quite respect either.

topics.label: who keeps a horse near this mound
topics.say: Rathe. I shoe what few horses Harrowfield's got left. Something about this mound makes every one of them balk, so I come see for myself what they already know.

topics.label: ask what the mound still wants
topics.say: Not shoes, and not prayers either. My guess is company. Whatever's down there hasn't had a living voice near it in longer than the ditch's been dug.

topics.label: offer a soldier's word over the tack
topics.say: You say what's said over a fallen mount, plain and short. Rathe doesn't ask where you learned it. Some words travel further than the unit that taught them.

sh_bonehouse_sabin.name: Sabin
sh_bonehouse_sabin.desc: A Harrowfield local with a small trowel and no particular hurry, tidying leaf-litter off a step nobody else troubles to clear.

topics.label: who tends the older bone-house
topics.say: Sabin. My grandfather's bones are in there with the rest of the fever dead. Elgin tends the new chantry. Nobody tends this one, so I do, when I remember to.

topics.label: ask what Elgin never says
topics.say: Nothing, is the trouble. Forty years of nothing said is its own kind of answer, if you know how to listen for the shape of it.

topics.label: read the stacking for who was last
topics.say: You read the courses the way you'd read a season's growth rings: the newest bones sit apart, stacked by a hand in less of a hurry than the ones before it.

sh_founders_camp_corin.name: Corin
sh_founders_camp_corin.desc: A recruiting officer's aide at the stakes, tally-slate under one arm, watching the gap in the fire-ring's smoke more than he watches you.

topics.label: why he's posted at the founders' stakes
topics.say: Corin. Recruiting officer's aide. I mind the stakes and the tally; she minds the fire and the terms. Long as you're not here for trouble, neither of us minds you.

topics.label: ask what terms she's really offering
topics.say: He gives it up slower than you'd like: fewer names sign than the founding charter needs, and every season the terms get a little more generous.

topics.label: trade watch-craft at the stakes
topics.say: He listens closer than he lets on, and moves the nearest stake a half-foot before you're even done talking. Old habits, he says, when you notice.

sh_levy.name: field-wight
sh_levy.desc: Gray as frost and just as cold to look at, holding a stance no living soldier could keep this long: shield up, feet set, waiting on an order that was never given to stand down.
onDeath: It goes down the way a held breath finally goes out, gray fading from the air where it stood. Somewhere across the plain, for a moment, the rest of the line seems to notice.
